entries.test: The scope of federal laws and remaining enforceable regulations would show whether barring state AI regulation leaves the AI industry mostly unregulated.
entries.note: This asserts a consequence of preemption, not that preemption has already occurred.
What qualifies as an acceptable excuse is an evaluative judgment. He does not assert that competition with China is the administration's actual motive.

Observation fits the polling component, but the record bundles it with a hedged forecast. The polling component could be checked separately; 'I doubt' prevents a settled test of the whole proposition.

entries.test: The executive order's legal effect and the federal, state, and judicial remedies available by the end of the publication week would show whether Americans retained substantial protection against AI harms.
entries.note: The deadline has passed. The surrounding discussion gives 'protection' a plain legal and regulatory meaning.

entries.test: Public market data and business reporting by the end of the publication week would show whether H200 sales to China harmed the commercial or competitive position of American AI companies other than Nvidia.
entries.note: The shared opening deadline reasonably applies to both clauses. 'Take a hit' has a plain meaning of commercial or competitive harm in this context.
